top5.title: Nvidia Suspends Server Shipments to Southeast Asia
top5.description: Nvidia reportedly asked server manufacturers to halt deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new U.S. export rules took effect. Fitch expects slower growth and more selective investment in the region’s data centers.
top5.why: Nvidia’s shipment halt across Southeast Asia shows that tightening U.S. export controls are already disrupting regional data-center investment and the global AI infrastructure supply chain.

top5.title: SAP considers cutting 10,000 jobs in AI-related restructuring
top5.description: SAP is considering eliminating at least 10,000 positions, or about 9% of its global workforce, as part of a shift toward artificial intelligence. No final plan has been decided, and discussions with employee representatives are ongoing.
top5.why: SAP’s potential elimination of at least 10,000 jobs signals that major enterprise software companies are restructuring materially around AI-driven productivity and changing demand.

top5.title: Soaring memory prices push companies to open “war rooms”
top5.description: The global memory chip shortage is prompting small companies in particular to create purchasing task forces to find DRAM, sometimes on eBay. Prices have risen 500%, while manufacturers are prioritizing HBM memory for AI.
top5.why: Memory prices rising as much as 500% confirms that AI demand is creating a broader semiconductor supply shock, increasing costs and procurement risks for companies.

top5.title: 42 Attorneys General Oppose the Sale of Character.AI Conversations
top5.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 U.S. attorneys general is trying to block the planned sale of conversation histories from more than 21 million accounts. It criticizes the lack of safeguards allowing users to delete data or requiring buyers to follow privacy policies.
top5.why: The bipartisan effort by 42 U.S. attorneys general to block Character.AI’s data sale could establish important privacy precedents for monetizing AI conversation histories.

top5.title: Hackers infiltrate the US Air Force’s main cloud platform
top5.description: Hackers exploited a vulnerability to access the control plane of Cloud One, the US Air Force’s cloud platform. The intrusion froze migrations and some software fixes, while US Cyber Command assesses the damage.
top5.why: The breach of the U.S. Air Force’s main cloud platform highlights the operational and national-security consequences of vulnerabilities in government cloud infrastructure.
